fits.equation_as_published: sigma = [A + B*eps_p^n][1 + C ln(epsdot*)][1 - T*^m]
fits.units_note: A and B in MPa. Tmelt 856 K is from the Al-Badour et al. 2014 table as reproduced in the JMSG paper. Tref 293 K is from the iSALE wiki/Pierazzo et al. 2008. The reference strain rate is not stated in the secondary sources opened; it is usually 1 s^-1 in JC tables, but that was NOT verified here.

fits.valid_range: not stated in the secondary sources

fits.citation: Widely re-tabulated set. Seen in: (1) Al-Badour et al. 2014 as reproduced in Table 4 of 'Effects of tool offset, pin offset, and alloys position on maximum temperature in dissimilar FSW of AA6061 and AA5086', J. Mater. Sci.: Mater. Eng. (Springer Open, 2020); (2) Table 3 of 'Milling Force Model for Aviation Aluminum Alloy: Academic Insight and Perspective Analysis', Chin. J. Mech. Eng. (2021) [their ref 106]; (3) Pierazzo et al. 2008, Meteoritics & Planetary Science 43:1917-1938 (iSALE benchmark). arXiv:2304.05231 attributes the set to Lesuer, Kay & LeBlanc, 'Modeling large-strain, high-rate deformation in metals', LLNL UCRL-JC-134118 (2001), but its text is corrupted and gives A = 334 MPa (probably an OCR or typo for 324).
fits.location: JMSG Table 4 (AA6061 row); CJME Table 3 (https://cjme.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s10033-021-00536-9/tables/3); iSALE wiki (https://github-wiki-see.page/m/isale-code/isale-wiki/wiki/Cratering-in-Aluminum-6061)
fits.notes: This is the de facto standard 6061-T6 JC set, and three independent secondary sources agree on A/B/n/C/m. The primary report (Lesuer et al. UCRL-JC-134118, or Johnson & Holmquist 1989 LA-11463-MS) could not be opened, so the original table/page is unverified. B = 114 MPa with n = 0.42 gives very low hardening (flow stress about 382 MPa at eps_p = 0.2), which is reasonable for 6061-T6. The low C = 0.002 means near rate-insensitivity.

fits.equation_as_published: sigma_Y = [A + B*eps_p_bar^n][1 + epsdot*]^C [1 - (T*)^m]  (modified JC, power-law rate term, Kang et al. 1999 form; Eq. 2)
fits.units_note: MPa. The rate term is the POWER-LAW form (1+epsdot*)^C, not the logarithmic form, so C is not interchangeable with log-form JC C values. Temperature term not used.
fits.valid_range: quasi-static tensile data at 0.01 s^-1 for A, B, n; C from ball-impact energy method
fits.test_conditions: Room temperature; MTS-810 tensile tests at 0.01 s^-1 per ISO 26203-2; 6061-T6 plate 3/6/8 mm thick. Paper Table 3 gives E = 68.3 GPa, nu = 0.33, rho = 2713 kg/m3

temper_check.notes: NASA-CR-123773 groups T6 and T651 under the same typical Ftu/Fty/elongation. AMS 4045 covers '7075-T6 sheet, -T651 plate'. Builders cutting wedges or armor from plate will nearly always get T651, which is stretch stress-relieved T6 with the same nominal properties. temper_check.recommended_default: AZ31B-H24 (cold rolled, partially annealed; AMS 4377): the standard sheet/plate temper sold by OnlineMetals and others. AZ31B-O is the annealed alternative.
temper_check.notes: The catalog strength values look like a MIX of spec minimums and typical values, not a consistent typical set. AMS 4377 minimums for 0.016-0.249 in sheet: UTS 39 ksi (269 MPa), TYS 29 ksi (200 MPa), elongation 6%. Strength minimums fall with thickness: 0.5-1.0 in gives 36/22 ksi = 248/152 MPa. The catalog's sy = 200 equals the thin-sheet minimum, but su = 260 is BELOW the thin-sheet minimum (269 MPa), and elong = 0.15 is a typical, not minimum, value. Suggested typical set: sy about 214 MPa (31 ksi), su about 290 MPa (42 ksi), elong about 0.16. Suggested conservative minimum set: sy 200, su 269, elong 0.06. For thick plate, use the thickness-dependent minimums. CRITICAL for simulation: wrought AZ31B is strongly tension/compression asymmetric because of twinning, with compressive yield well below tensile yield in the rolling plane, plus anisotropy. A single isotropic von Mises curve will mispredict compression-dominated contact.

temper_check.recommended_default: Keep AR500 (generic through-hardened ~500 BHN quench-and-temper wear plate). Catalog yield 1250 / UTS 1640 / 8% sits within the published range: Armox 500T supplier minimums (Rp0.2 >= 1250, Rm 1450-1750, A5 >= 8%) and Chapel AR500F typicals (yield 187 ksi = 1289 MPa, UTS 247 ksi = 1703 MPa). temper_check.notes: AR500 is not a standardized grade; it is a distributor/mill hardness designation (BHN 477-534 nominal by some vendors; Chapel lists 470-530 typical, 450 min / 500 nominal). Hardox 500 hardness is 470-530 HBW (sheet 2-7 mm and plate 4-32 mm), 450-540 HBW for 32.1-103 mm, typical yield 1400 MPa (not guaranteed); SSAB's web page lists no UTS or elongation. Armox 500T is an armor grade (480-540 HBW) with tighter toughness specs. No published constitutive fit exists for generic 'AR500'; the nearest fits are for Armox 500T (same hardness class). Hardox 500 JC fits were not found in an openly readable source.

The catalog's 1450 / 1940 / 0.07 combines the 205 C row (yield 1450, 7%) with a UTS slightly below the 315 C row (1965). For a conservative but consistent set, use the 315 C / 55 HRC row: 1585 / 1965 / 0.09.
temper_check.notes: Hardness vs temper from vendor datasheets: Crucible DS314 (400 F: 55-58 HRC; 500 F: 54-56; 600 F: 53-55); SB Specialty Metals (400 F: 57; 500 F: 55; 600 F: 54); Abrams (572 F: 56 HRC; 392 F: 58). So 56 HRC is roughly a 205-300 C temper, depending on the source. No manufacturer datasheet found (Crucible, Industeel, SBSM, Abrams) lists tensile data vs temper. The only tensile table found is an ASM-style table reproduced on a distributor blog; it was not opened in a primary ASM source. Yield rising from the 205 C temper (1450) to the 315 C temper (1585) is real and typical of tool-steel stress relief, not a typo.

temper_check.recommended_default: Keep H900 (solution treated, aged 1 h at 482 C / 900 F). The catalog's 1170 / 1310 / 0.10 / HRC 40 are the specification minimums (AMS 5604/5643 / ASTM A564), not typical values. For a 'typical' sim card use ATI typicals: sy 1240 MPa, su 1340 MPa, elongation 10% in 2 in., HRC 43, E 196 GPa, rho 7810. Set hardness to 'HRC 40-47 (spec), 43-45 typical'.
temper_check.notes: The user's point is confirmed: H900 is typically HRC 43-45 (ATI typical 43; Wu & Lin 44.5; Boeing data HRc 45 / BHN 421). HRC 40 is only the specification floor (AMS 5604 lists 40-47 Rc). Other measured H900 values: BMI (Dunleavy & Spretnak, AFML-TR-68-353, as reproduced in BDX-613-577) UTS 200.4 ksi (1382 MPa), YS 178.6 ksi (1231 MPa); Boeing 1968 bar Su 1343, Sy 1103 MPa, 17% elongation (longitudinal), RA 53.5%; Wu & Lin Sy 1387, Su 1414 MPa, 12.5% elongation. fits.test_conditions: Aged 1 h at 900 F. Bendix: sheet 0.062/0.120/0.240 in., 0.04 in/min. BMI: 1/4 in. round bars, 0.01 in/min, room temperature.

The report shows a large spread (0.068 to 0.457) depending on specimen and extrapolation. Use only for large-strain extrapolation, or don't use it. Values were read through OCR.

open_raw_data.description: NIST dataset 'Compressive Stress-Strain Curves for Wrought and AM Precipitation-Hardenable Stainless Steel at Dynamic Strain Rates at Room Temperature and with Rapid Heating and at Low Strain Rates at Room Temperature' (Mates et al.). Wrought 17-4 in solutionized, H900 and H1150 conditions plus other aging treatments. Kolsky-bar compression (about 1300-4500/s, RT to about 1000 C with rapid heating) and servohydraulic compression (0.0003 and 0.03/s). CSV files of strain, stress, strain rate and initial temperature. temper_check.recommended_default: Keep '304 annealed'. The catalog values (E 193, sy 215, su 505, elongation 0.70) match the ASM Aerospace Specification Metals / MatWeb 'AISI Type 304' datasheet exactly (also HRB 70, nu 0.29, rho 8000, G 86 GPa). Consider rho 7900-8000 and E 193-200.
temper_check.notes: The ASM/MatWeb values are typical annealed-bar values. Real annealed 304 sheet/plate often runs higher (yield about 250-310, UTS about 580-650 MPa), and 505 MPa is slightly below the commonly cited ASTM A240 minimum of 515 MPa (not verified from an opened source in this pass). For impact sims, 304's large strain-rate sensitivity and strain-induced martensite hardening matter more than these quasi-static numbers. Wikipedia cites MIL-HDBK-5J p. 2-222 for E 183-200 GPa and rho 7900. MIL-HDBK-5 S-basis minimums for annealed 301/304 (AMS 5513): Ftu 73-75 ksi (503-517 MPa), Fty 26-30 ksi (179-207 MPa), e >= 40%, E 200 GPa, nu 0.27. So the catalog's 215/505 is close to the design-minimum level, which is conservative for strength.

Elongation 10% is plausible but unverified. Hardenability: every heat-treated 4130 row in the Alro table is water quenched (1575F), versus oil for 4140/4340, i.e. 4130 is shallow-hardening; thin sheet (a few mm) can through-harden but distortion and quench cracking are the practical risks. I did not open a Jominy/ideal-diameter source to quantify this.
